result.explanation: The mean fractal dimension is a measure of the complexity or irregularity of cell boundaries, and in pathological contexts, higher fractal dimension is typically associated with more complex, disordered tissue structures—commonly seen in malignant tumors. However, in both instances, the model is misclassifying despite the values having counterintuitive patterns: Instance 73 (malignant true, predicted benign) has a low mean fractal dimension (0.06566), and Instance 291 (benign true, predicted malignant) has a relatively low mean fractal dimension (0.05852). This low value is semantically implausible for a malignant classification, as malignancy is expected to show greater complexity. Conversely, benign cases, which are less structurally complex, naturally exhibit lower fractal dimension. The model's misclassification suggests it may be over-relying on this feature or misinterpreting its semantic contribution—indicating a possible spurious or misleading signal in the model's training. Thus, mean fractal dimension may be acting as a spurious feature due to its structural misalignment with clinical interpretation in these cases.
